title: First-order coherence of Bose condensates
lead: The classical, first-order coherence of a condensate: two clouds released together interfere into fringes, coherence in a thermal cloud reaches only about a deBroglie wavelength while a condensate's spans the cloud, as an atom laser measures, and two condensates of fixed atom number gain a relative phase only when their atoms are detected.
notes: Figure 11.12 is computed from a model; the book's image reproduces published data and is not shown.

figures.original_caption: By allowing two classically coherent condensates separated by a distance $\Delta R_s$ to expand and interfere, one can observe fringes spaced by $\Delta R \sim \hbar\tau/\Delta R_s m$. Experiments at MIT (c.f. Andrews et al., Science 275, p637 (2000)) observed these fringes. Two BECs, imaged in trap using phase-contrast imaging, were allowed to expand and interfere, producing interference fringes in the time-of-flight absorption image.

footnotes.html: The magnetic field gradient arises because the center of the trap is shifted from the magnetic field minimum by gravity, so the untrapped states have a position-dependent Zeeman energy.
The caption prints 2000 as the year. Andrews et al., “Observation of interference between two Bose condensates”, appeared in Science 275, 637 in 1997.
